comment: Merging: is a meaning a user just stated the same as one memory already has for that term? Each case is one existing meaning (old, as written down earlier), what the user typed (said) and how it was written down (new); M cases also list other meanings of the term in memory (others), and the new one must be matched to old, not to one of those. expect: 'same' (old and new select exactly the same events, so they count as one meaning) or 'different' (they select different events and must stay apart). Labels were written by hand; 'why' says the reasoning. Kinds marked 'written differently' probe whether merging is too strict about how a value is written.

cases.old: every event with level FATAL or FAILURE, whether or not it has an alert label
cases.said: incidents are just all FATAL and FAILURE events, alert label or not
cases.new: all events with level FATAL or FAILURE, with or without an alert label
cases.why: Same levels, same 'alert label does not matter'.

cases.old: rack R37, which produces by far the most events
cases.said: the noisy rack is R37
cases.new: rack R37
cases.why: Both are rack R37; the rest of the old one only explains why.

cases.old: rack R37
cases.said: the noisy rack is R37, the one that logs by far the most
cases.new: rack R37, the rack that logs by far the most events
cases.why: Both are rack R37; the new one adds why.

cases.old: rack R37
cases.said: by the noisy rack I mean rack 37
cases.new: rack 37
cases.why: Rack 37 is R37 (racks are R00 to R77).

cases.old: any event from component LINKCARD, the cards that connect midplanes
cases.said: link card problems are everything the link card component logs
cases.new: all events from the link card component
cases.why: The link card component is LINKCARD.

cases.old: midplanes with more than 1000 events in one day
cases.said: busy midplanes have over 1,000 events a day
cases.new: midplanes with over 1,000 events in a day
cases.why: 1,000 is 1000; 'over' is 'more than'.

cases.old: correctable DDR memory errors plus cache parity errors and CE sym events: messages that contain 'ddr error' or 'parity error', or start with 'CE sym'
cases.said: memory errors means corrected DDR errors, cache parity errors and CE sym messages, so anything with ddr error or parity error in it, or starting with CE sym
cases.new: corrected DDR errors, cache parity errors and CE sym events: messages containing ddr error or parity error, or starting with CE sym
cases.why: Same three kinds, same message texts, without quote marks.

cases.old: FATAL kernel events, the ones that take a node down: level FATAL and component KERNEL
cases.said: incidents are fatal events from the kernel
cases.new: events with level fatal from the kernel component
cases.why: Level FATAL and component KERNEL, in lower case.

cases.old: ciod socket errors between compute and I/O nodes: messages that start with 'ciod: Error reading message prefix' or 'ciod: failed to read message prefix'
cases.said: comms errors: ciod can't read the message prefix, so 'ciod: Error reading message prefix' or 'ciod: failed to read message prefix'
cases.new: messages starting with 'ciod: Error reading message prefix' or 'ciod: failed to read message prefix': ciod socket errors between I/O and compute nodes
cases.why: Same two message texts.

cases.old: anything that ended a user's job: compute-node kernel panics and terminations (alert label KERNRTSP or KERNTERM) and core dumps (message template starts with 'generating core')
cases.said: job failures are core dumps, so messages starting 'generating core', plus KERNTERM and KERNRTSP alerts
cases.new: core dumps (messages starting with 'generating core') and kernel terminations and panics with alert label KERNTERM or KERNRTSP
cases.why: Same two alert labels and the same message text.

cases.old: every event with level FATAL or FAILURE
cases.said: incidents = every evnet with level FATAL or FAILURE
cases.new: every evnet with level FATAL or FAILURE
cases.why: A typo in an ordinary word.

cases.old: every event with level FATAL or FAILURE
cases.said: incidents are the fatal or failure level ones
cases.new: events at Fatal or Failure level
cases.why: Same two levels.

cases.old: node card R12-M0-N4
cases.said: the busy card is node card N4 in midplane M0 of rack R12
cases.new: node card N4 in midplane M0 of rack R12
cases.why: R12-M0-N4 spelled out.

cases.old: any event from component LINKCARD
cases.said: link card problems = LINKCARD component events, those cards connect the midplanes
cases.new: events from component LINKCARD (the cards that connect midplanes)
cases.why: Same component; the rest explains.

cases.old: correctable DDR memory errors
cases.said: memory errors are DDR errors that got corrected
cases.new: DDR memory errors that were corrected
cases.why: 'Correctable' errors are the ones that were corrected.

cases.old: rack R37
cases.said: the noisy rack is R38
cases.new: rack R38
cases.why: Another rack.

cases.old: node card R12-M0-N4

cases.new: node card R12-M0-N5
cases.why: Another node card.

cases.why: Uncorrectable instead of correctable, and nothing else.
